pages.text: Early one morning, Safiatu walked to the community borehole with her older brother Hammond. A neat line of neighbours was already waiting with their buckets. Safiatu sighed. “We will be waiting here all day!”
sentences: Early one morning, Safiatu walked to the community borehole with her older brother Hammond.
A neat line of neighbours was already waiting with their buckets.
Safiatu sighed.
“We will be waiting here all day!”
pages.alt: In morning sunlight, Safiatu with her small yellow bucket and Hammond with his larger blue bucket arrive at the back of an orderly village borehole queue.

pages.text: “Let us slip up to the front,” she whispered. Hammond shook his head gently. “Everyone ahead of us arrived earlier, and every family needs clean water. A fair queue respects everyone—we join at the back and wait our turn.”
sentences: “Let us slip up to the front,” she whispered.
Hammond shook his head gently.
“Everyone ahead of us arrived earlier, and every family needs clean water.
A fair queue respects everyone—we join at the back and wait our turn.”
pages.alt: Safiatu pointing eagerly toward the front of the borehole queue while calm Hammond shakes his head kindly beside their buckets.

pages.text: Soon an elderly grandmother arrived carrying a heavy bucket, looking tired. Together, the neighbours at the front cheerfully invited her to fill hers first. “That is kindness,” said Hammond. “Everyone in line agreed together, so it stayed fair.”
sentences: Soon an elderly grandmother arrived carrying a heavy bucket, looking tired.
Together, the neighbours at the front cheerfully invited her to fill hers first.
“That is kindness,” said Hammond.
“Everyone in line agreed together, so it stayed fair.”
pages.alt: Friendly neighbours at the front of the borehole queue smiling and making room so a grateful elderly woman in traditional cloth can fill her bucket first.

pages.text: Safiatu looked along the row of buckets ahead of them and counted aloud: “Fourteen.” To pass the time cheerfully, she played a quiet finger-counting game with a little girl beside her. Before long, only three buckets remained ahead of them!
sentences: Safiatu looked along the row of buckets ahead of them and counted aloud: “Fourteen.” To pass the time cheerfully, she played a quiet finger-counting game with a little girl beside her.
Before long, only three buckets remained ahead of them!
pages.alt: In the sunny queue, smiling Safiatu plays a cheerful finger-counting game with a happy toddler standing beside her mother.

pages.text: At last it was their turn. Hammond worked the pump handle steadily while Safiatu held her yellow bucket right beneath the spout. As soon as it reached the brim, they stopped the water at once so none spilled. “Every drop is precious,” said Safiatu.
sentences: At last it was their turn.
Hammond worked the pump handle steadily while Safiatu held her yellow bucket right beneath the spout.
As soon as it reached the brim, they stopped the water at once so none spilled.
“Every drop is precious,” said Safiatu.
pages.alt: At the concrete borehole pad, Hammond pumps the metal handle while Safiatu holds her yellow bucket carefully beneath the clear stream of water.

pages.text: Walking home together, Safiatu smiled at Hammond. “Waiting our turn was not bad after all.” “Patience gave us time to be kind and make a friend,” agreed Hammond. At home, they poured the clean water into a covered storage pot.
sentences: Walking home together, Safiatu smiled at Hammond.
“Waiting our turn was not bad after all.” “Patience gave us time to be kind and make a friend,” agreed Hammond.
At home, they poured the clean water into a covered storage pot.
pages.alt: Inside their clean family courtyard, Safiatu and Hammond pour clear water carefully into a tidy lidded storage container.

activities.question: Why did Hammond say they must join the back of the queue?
options: Everyone ahead had already been waiting fairly
He wanted to spill the water

activities.question: What did Safiatu and Hammond do as soon as the bucket was full?
options: Stopped the water at once so none was wasted
Tipped the bucket onto the ground

Very valuable and worthy of careful protection, never to be wasted.
